scope: Standard QCAA General and General (Extension) sequences represented in the EA game, plus the two Applied (Essential) CIAs. Other Applied subjects and alternative sequences are not mapped here.

subjects.subject: legal
subjects.name: Legal Studies
topics: Democracy, the rule of law and government accountability
Separation of powers and judicial independence
Division of powers and constitutional inconsistency
Parliament: structure, roles and the legislative process
The High Court and constitutional interpretation
Precedent, statutory interpretation and landmark decisions
Governance issues: viewpoints, consequences and legal alternatives
subjects.note: Short responses assess comprehension; the extended response uses unseen stimulus for analysis and evaluation. Use cases taught in your course; syllabus examples are not a universal compulsory case list.

resources.name: Parliamentary Education Office: government and parliament

subjects.subject: economics
subjects.name: Economics
topics: Australia’s trade patterns and trade theories
Balance of payments: accounts and relationships
Trade data: patterns, trends and economic relationships
Evaluating international-trade outcomes using economic criteria
subjects.note: Includes multiple choice, short responses and one extended response to unseen stimulus. Global economic issues in Topic 2 are the IA2 investigation focus. Use fresh practice materials; the syllabus prohibits rehearsing the exam questions in class.

subjects.subject: business
subjects.name: Business
topics: Domestic and global expansion strategies and modes of entry
Leadership, risk management and human resource strategies
SWOT and power interest grid analysis
Asian expansion case study and strategy evaluation
subjects.note: Restrict revision to Topic 1; Topic 2 Strategic development is assessed through the business report.

resources.name: business.gov.au: managing change
resources.note: Use a practical Australian change-management example to connect planning, stakeholder involvement and communication with business transformation.

subjects.subject: accounting
subjects.name: Accounting
topics: Acquiring non-current assets and classifying expenditure
Disposal of non-current assets and gain or loss
subjects.note: Includes short, practical and extended responses. Cash management in Topic 1 is the IA1 project focus.

resources.name: AccountingCoach: explanations
resources.note: Revise double-entry accounting, adjustments, statements and financial ratios. US examples use some different terms and formats; follow the conventions in your class materials.
resources.access: Free explanations; some additional tools are paid

subjects.subject: atsi_studies
subjects.name: Aboriginal & Torres Strait Islander Studies
topics: Responses to government policies and restrictions
Interpreting sources and perspectives on rights and freedoms
subjects.note: Use the communities, events and source contexts studied in your course. Avoid generalising one community’s experience to all First Nations peoples.
subjects.context: Community, event or case study taught in class

resources.name: AIATSIS: explore
resources.note: Explore First Nations histories and recognition, including the 1967 Referendum and Freedom Ride. Use evidence from the relevant community and historical context.

subjects.subject: ancient_history
subjects.name: Ancient History
topics: Chronology and context of the selected ancient society
Developing a historical argument from sources
subjects.note: An essay responds to an unseen question using seen and unseen sources. The school selects the historical topic. Do not use secure assessment sources for guided practice.
subjects.context: Your IA1 ancient society and aspect

resources.name: History Skills: source analysis and evaluation
resources.note: Revise how to analyse origin, purpose, perspective and evidence, then judge usefulness and reliability. Practise with sources from your school-selected EA topic.

resources.name: World History Encyclopedia: education
resources.note: Search for your selected ancient personality or civilisation to review context, chronology and historical interpretations.
resources.access: Free articles and teaching resources; optional membership is paid

resources.name: History Skills: source analysis and evaluation
resources.note: Revise how to analyse origin, purpose, perspective and evidence, then judge usefulness and reliability. Practise with sources from your school-selected EA topic.
